summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — HPE +19%, COHR +18%, LITE +14%, GLW +13%, CIEN +10%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (TTD -9%, INTU -9%, CBOE -8%, CVNA -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HPE (+19.47%) — Q2 2026 earnings blowout — revenue $10.7B (+40% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.79 (+108%), FY EPS guide raised to $3.35–$3.45 from $2.30–$2.50; $1.8B in new AI server orders and Juniper synergies ahead of plan. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — HPE is a large-cap S&P 500 AI-infrastructure name (~$50B+ market cap) excluded by sector/cap filters. Earnings were reported after hours Jun 1–2, so capturing the peak gap required pre-open positioning before any intraday signal fired.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings blowout — revenue $10.7B (+40% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.79 (+108%), FY EPS guide raised to $3.35–$3.45 from $2.30–$2.50; $1.8B in new AI server orders and Juniper synergies ahead of plan.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HPE is a large-cap S&P 500 AI-infrastructure name (~$50B+ market cap) excluded by sector/cap filters. Earnings were reported after hours Jun 1–2, so capturing the peak gap required pre-open positioning before any intraday signal fired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap-capture module: large-caps (≥$5B market cap) with a post-results open gap ≥15% enter a single-session momentum long, bypassing standard universe exclusions for that day only.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 FY2026 EPS of $1.41 beat consensus on revenue +27% YoY; Nvidia simultaneously disclosed a $2B equity stake and multiyear AI-optics supply agreement, triggering analyst target hikes across 8 firms.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. COHR is a large-cap AI-optics name not covered by any strategy; the +17% gap combined an earnings beat with Nvidia's $2B equity stake deal — requiring pre-market positioning the bot cannot take.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap-up scanner that flags non-universe names with ADV ≥$200M gapping ≥+10% on earnings day; allow momentum entry within 30 min of open if volume confirms ≥1.5× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly endorsed optical interconnects ('use optics where you must') at a major event, sparking a sector re-rate for optical suppliers; LITE had also posted a beat-and-raise Q3 on May 5 (revenue +90% YoY, EPS $2.37 vs $2.17 est).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LITE is a large-cap optical-networking stock (~$1,029/share, ~$35B market cap). The move was Nvidia CEO-comment-driven, requiring pre-market sector monitoring; no intraday momentum filter triggers before a gap of this size has fully run.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an optical/photonics sector basket (LITE, COHR, GLW) to the news-reactive strategy's universe with a hyperscaler-CEO-endorsement trigger: release names gapping ≥8% within 15 minutes of open on AI-infrastructure headline events.

top_movers.catalyst: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Computex commentary on AI-datacenter optical interconnects, plus Corning's own investor-day guidance raise to $30B annualized revenue exiting 2028 (19% CAGR), drove a >13% single-day gap.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. GLW is a large-cap AI-infrastructure materials name (fiber/optical glass); the move was jointly triggered by a third-party keynote and a pre-announced investor day — both pre-event signals that post-open momentum or mean-reversion filters cannot capture after the gap is printed.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend the momentum strategy's universe to include large-cap AI-infrastructure materials names (e.g., fiber/optical-component SIC screen); a gap-up filter of ≥8% at open with ≥1.5× avg volume would have flagged GLW for a disciplined partial entry today.

top_movers.catalyst: B. Riley doubled price target ($283→$531), new cloud/subsea contracts signed with Cirion and Biznet announced, and pre-earnings positioning ahead of Q2 report due June 4 (consensus: $1.46 EPS, +248% YoY).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe; CIEN is a large-cap optical networking name (~$627, P/E ~400×) likely excluded by valuation screens. Move was earnings-eve pre-positioning requiring pre-market catalyst detection to capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a pre-earnings catalyst scanner: flag names with analyst PT upgrades ≥40% or new contract filings within 72h of scheduled earnings; release for momentum entry if pre-market gap ≥5% on volume ≥1.5× avg.

top_movers.catalyst: Deeply oversold life-science REIT continued a ~27%-over-one-month mean-reversion rally on broad REIT sector tailwind from rate-cut expectations; no discrete company-specific news on June 3.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ARE is an S&P 500 life-science REIT in a structural downtrend (45% dividend cut, ongoing $1.8B asset sales); persistent negative price trend excludes it from both momentum and news-reactive filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a distressed-large-cap mean-reversion screen: S&P 500 members >35% below 52-week high with ≥+5% 1-month relative strength vs. their sector ETF, gate-opened after ≥2 consecutive up weeks.

top_movers.catalyst: Ongoing Publicis fallout: a leaked client email revealed TTD failed a third-party fee audit ('violated multiple clauses'), with Dentsu and WPP also retreating from OpenPath; broader adtech sector weakness amplified the sell-off.
top_movers.miss_reason: TTD is outside any active strategy's universe. Down 43% YTD on Publicis dispute (>10% gross billings at risk) and Chrome cookie-deprecation headwinds — it sits below momentum entry thresholds and is too open-ended a falling-knife for mean-reversion long filters.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable long-side change; if short capability is added later, a structural-deterioration filter (≥2 major agency relationship breaks AND analyst revenue-cut within 60 days) would have flagged TTD as a short candidate well before this leg down.

top_movers.catalyst: Goldman Sachs downgraded INTU to Sell from Hold on June 2, citing intensifying AI-driven competition in consumer tax filing, triggering a ~9% two-day selloff into June 3's close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — INTU is a large-cap (~$85B) software/fintech name likely excluded by sector or cap-tier filters. The move was a broker-downgrade catalyst that requires a sell-side signal feed and short capability to trade; post-open momentum entry would chase a gap already >5% wide.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a bulge-bracket-downgrade scanner to the news-reactive strategy: if a major broker cuts to Sell with a price-target drop ≥10% on a large-cap software name, gate it for short consideration within the first 30 min of open — requires enabling short capability for this ticker class.

top_movers.catalyst: CFTC approved Kalshi's Bitcoin perpetual futures, triggering sector-wide selloff in exchange operators (CBOE, CME, ICE) on fears that perpetual futures could expand to other asset classes and erode derivatives market share.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CBOE is a large-cap financial-exchange operator not covered by typical equity momentum/mean-reversion universes. The driver was a regulatory sector shock (competition threat), not a company-specific earnings or M&A event, making pre-market positioning via standard signals imposs
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap exchange operators (CBOE, CME, ICE) to a news-reactive short-side watchlist; gate entries on regulatory/competition headlines scored by a news-sentiment filter, releasing a short signal only when sector-wide volume confirms the catalyst within 30 min of open.

top_movers.catalyst: CFO Mark Jenkins and BHJC Trust filed Form 144 SEC disclosures on June 1 proposing 113K+ share sales; combined with lingering Q1 EBITDA margin-contraction fears and a broker downgrade to neutral, this broke post-earnings support.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CVNA is high-beta used-car retail already -27% YTD; the trigger was Form 144 insider-intent-to-sell SEC filings — a regulatory signal that standard price/volume momentum filters cannot detect before the move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a Form 144 filing monitor: flag S&P 1500 names with >50K insider-proposed shares in a rolling 5-day window as a short-side catalyst gate, bypassing universe filters for a 1-day event trade (requires short capability to act on).
